summary: Research how strategy games make wars legible: unit info, battle windows, casualty reporting, intel estimates

reports.topic: War information design for map-scale force display: counter anatomy, progressive disclosure, battle-outcome visualization, and loss/provenance reporting — synthesized from HoI4, Unity of Command, NATO symbology, War in the East, Panzer Corps, and DEFCON

findings.name: Counter anatomy: the NATO counter is the correct base layer, not sprites
findings.detail: Classic NATO symbology (per APP-6 and every hex wargame since the 60s) packs four channels into one rectangle: (1) fill/frame color = affiliation (friendly blue/national color, hostile red), (2) an inner glyph = unit type (infantry = X saltire, armor = oval/tread, artillery = filled dot, mechanized = saltire over oval), (3) size designator above the frame (II battalion, III regiment, X brigade, XX division, XXX corps), (4) strength/movement numbers along the bottom edge (War in the East uses 'attack-movement' e.g. 9-18, or 'attack=defense' 1=3 for enemies, and '?-?' when undetected). This was designed to be hand-drawable and monochrome-readable — i.e., it survives being 24px tall on a busy map. HoI4's community overwhelmingly mods toward this (MPU Map Counters, DzK Better Counters: 'bigger ORG/STR bar, group icon, unit count, flag and unit symbol... best used with NATO symbols enabled').
findings.recommendation: Replace 'small colored boxes with a count' with a proper counter: 28x28px (at 1x zoom) rounded-rect filled with nation color, 1px darker border; centered 14px white NATO glyph for the stack's dominant unit type; stack count as a 9-10px bold numeral in the top-right corner on a 12px dark pill; size designator (X/XX/XXX) as 6px text above the frame only when zoomed in. Selected state: 2px white outline + 20% brightness lift; hovered: 1px white outline. Never rely on color alone — glyph + count must read in grayscale.

findings.name: The HoI4 dual-bar (strength + organization) is the single highest-value element to copy
findings.detail: HoI4 counters attach two tiny bars to every stack: a horizontal green STRENGTH bar along the bottom (manpower/equipment HP) and a vertical ORG bar on the left edge (will-to-fight; drains first, breaks the division when empty). Players call this 'tremendously useful' because at a glance across a 40-province front you can see which sectors are fresh (both bars full) vs. brittle (org nearly empty) without clicking anything. Your combat model is literally cohesion-vs-strength, so the mapping is one-to-one. Community counter mods' #1 change is making these bars BIGGER and adding tick marks — Paradox made them too thin (~2px).
findings.recommendation: Add two bars to every province counter: bottom horizontal bar = average strength (3px tall, full counter width, green >66% / yellow 33-66% / red <33%), left vertical bar = average cohesion (3px wide, full counter height, same color ramp but rendered in a cooler hue family so the two are distinguishable, e.g. strength green-ramp, cohesion cyan→orange). Add 25% tick marks (1px darker notches). For enemy counters show the same bars but quantized to thirds and dimmed 30% (intel-fuzzed — see fog finding). This alone answers half of 'why am I losing': the player sees org collapse propagate along the front in real time.

findings.name: Unity of Command's chips are praised because strength is COUNTABLE OBJECTS, not a number
findings.detail: UoC's universally loved unit chip shows strength as discrete 'steps' — a row of up to 7 tiny soldier/tank figures on the chip itself. Combat doesn't subtract an invisible HP pool; it visibly greys/dims suppressed steps and removes killed ones, so after an attack you literally see '2 of his 6 steps are suppressed, attack again now.' Specialist attachments (AT, engineers) render as differently-shaped figures appended to the row. Reviews single out that it 'displays information about the units in a clean and simple manner, using icons to indicate damage, entrenchment, movement status, the supply situation' and that you never 'fight the game tooth-and-nail for every shred of information' (gamedeveloper.com case study). The lesson: at map scale, discrete pips beat both raw numbers and analog bars for legibility, because humans subitize up to ~5-7 objects instantly.
findings.recommendation: At close zoom (or on hover), expand the counter into a chip ~64x40px: nation-color plate, NATO glyph left, then one pip per division (max ~8, then '+N'): filled pip = healthy, half-faded pip = low cohesion, hollow pip = shattered/recovering. During an active battle, animate pips dimming as cohesion drains — this converts your hourly tick math into visible attrition. Keep the 28px counter for far zoom; the pip chip is the mid-zoom/hover state.

findings.name: Three-tier progressive disclosure: counter → hover card → click panel (War in the East model)
findings.detail: WitE explicitly layers: (tier 1) the counter itself with color/symbol/size/two numbers, plus optional 'soft factor' corner pips flagging supply/fuel/morale problems 'at a glance'; (tier 2) hover tooltip with the unit list and exact values; (tier 3) click-through to a full unit detail screen with TOE, losses, history. Crucially the bottom numbers are TOGGLEABLE (attack/move vs attack/defense vs name) — the player chooses which scalar matters right now. HoI4 does the same: counter → hover shows division list with individual org/str bars → click opens the division/army panel.
findings.recommendation: Implement exactly three tiers. Tier 1 (always, map): counter + count + bars as specced above, plus at most ONE alert pip (6px triangle, top-left): red = out of supply, orange = cohesion <25%, white = reinforcing. Tier 2 (hover, <100ms, no click): 220px card listing each division as a row [type glyph | name | strength bar | cohesion bar | terrain/entrenchment icon], plus 'Arriving: 2 divisions, 14h' if reinforcements are en route. Tier 3 (click): full province military panel with per-division stats, modifiers, and orders. Rule of thumb: tier 1 answers 'where is the problem', tier 2 answers 'what is here', tier 3 answers 'what do I do'.

findings.name: Battles must exist as on-map objects with a predicted winner (HoI4 battle bubble)
findings.detail: In HoI4 every active combat spawns a bubble icon on the province border: crossed-swords glyph inside a circular gauge that fills green (winning) or red (losing) based on predicted outcome, so a paused player can sweep the whole front and triage which fights need attention. Clicking the bubble opens the combat window. Without this, real-time combat is invisible until provinces flip — which is exactly the director's 'seems like magic' complaint applied to battles. DEFCON proves the minimal end works too: pure thin vector glyphs + expanding rings for hits on a dark map, everything readable at a glance with zero text.
findings.recommendation: Spawn a battle marker at the contested-province edge for every active combat: 20px circle, crossed-swords glyph, ringed by a 2.5px arc gauge — arc sweeps clockwise green for attacker advantage, counterclockwise red, derived from (attacker cohesion-delta rate vs defender's) so it's an honest projection of your tick math. Pulse the ring (0.8s scale 1.0→1.15) while the battle is 'hot' (tick just resolved). Hover = mini combat card (both sides' totals + top 2 modifiers); click = full combat window. This is the highest-leverage single feature for 'watching a war'.

findings.name: 'Why am I losing' = a signed modifier ledger, attacker vs defender, every number hoverable
findings.detail: HoI4's combat window is two mirrored columns (attacker left, defender right): each side shows total soldiers, a stack of division rows each with its own org/strength bars, and — the critical part — a modifier breakdown reachable by hover: a vertical list of signed percentages, green positive / red negative ('Terrain: -40%', 'River crossing: -30%', 'Enemy entrenchment: -25%', 'Air superiority: +10%'), summing to the final attack value. Paradox's rule that every displayed number decomposes on hover is the accepted genre answer to 'why am I losing'. You already compute terrain/home/quality modifiers hourly — they are currently invisible.
findings.recommendation: Build the combat window as two columns with a center gutter. Per side: flag, total troops, aggregate strength+cohesion bars, division list. Center: the projected-outcome gauge (same as the map bubble, larger) and hourly loss rates for BOTH sides. Below each side: modifier ledger — one row per active modifier, icon + name + signed % , green/red, sorted by absolute magnitude, with the net multiplier at the bottom in bold. Do not hide this behind hover on v1 — print the top 5 directly in the window; the director's complaint says the info is missing, not that the window is cluttered. Add one synthesized line at top: 'Losing: enemy entrenchment (-25%) and river crossing (-30%) outweigh your quality edge (+15%).' — a plain-language verdict computed from the largest terms.

findings.name: 'Where troops come from' = draw movement as arrows and reinforcements as explicit arrivals
findings.detail: Troops 'appearing by magic' is a provenance problem: the player never sees movement orders, transit, or deployment. HoI4 solves it three ways: (1) unit movement renders as an arrow from origin to destination with a progress bulge, visible for ENEMY units too (you watch the arrow coming); (2) frontline/offensive plans draw persistent arrows so the shape of an operation is visible before and during execution; (3) new divisions appear only via an explicit deployment act at a chosen location. UoC's equivalent lesson is its supply overlay — the flow that feeds the front can be made visible as an overlay when it matters.
findings.recommendation: Render every in-transit army as (a) a ghost counter at 55% opacity at its current interpolated position, and (b) a 2px arrow from origin to destination in the nation color, with elapsed portion solid and remaining portion dashed; show ETA in hours on hover. Apply this to VISIBLE enemy armies too — enemy redeployment arrows are precisely what kills 'magic'. When reinforcements join a battle or garrison, fire a one-shot animation: small counter flies in along the arrow and merges, plus a '+2 divisions' toast above the province for 3s. Add a 'flows' map mode later if needed; arrows on the default mode are the v1.

findings.name: Enemy losses and fog: show estimates as fuzzy values with visible confidence (WitE detection model)
findings.detail: War in the East displays enemy counters with estimated values ('X=Y') that sharpen with detection level, and '?-?' when undetected — the display itself communicates intel quality. HoI4 gates counter detail behind decryption/intel: without intel you see a generic counter, with it you see composition. For loss ESTIMATES, HoI4's war overview screen shows cumulative casualties per belligerent (yours exact, theirs intel-derived). The principle: never show enemy numbers at the same precision as your own, and make the imprecision visible rather than silently wrong.
findings.recommendation: Track true enemy losses per war; display them through an intel filter: estimate = true value × noise factor sampled once per war-update (not per frame), rendered as a range at low intel ('~8,000–12,000 killed'), a single rounded figure at high intel ('~9,400'). Same for enemy counters: no intel → counter shows glyph + '?' instead of count and no bars; partial → count quantized (1-3/4-8/9+) and bars in thirds; full → near-exact. In the combat window print enemy hourly losses as 'est.' with a tilde. Cheap to implement (you already know truth; just add noise + rounding tiers) and it makes scouting/intel a real mechanic later.

findings.name: Aggregate army numbers: a persistent war HUD, not a buried panel
findings.detail: HoI4 gives per-army totals on selection banners (divisions, avg org/str) and a war overview with casualties, warscore, and participation per side. The director wants 'overall army numbers' while WATCHING — meaning the totals must live on screen during a war, not two clicks deep. Sports-scoreboard framing (DEFCON's kill-counter endgame is the extreme case) is what makes a war feel legible: two numbers, a trend, and a delta.
findings.recommendation: When any war is active, dock a war ribbon at top of the war-room panel (or top-center of screen): [your flag] 312k troops · 41 divs ⟷ [their flag] ~280k · ~36 divs, plus cumulative losses both sides (yours exact, theirs est.), plus a thin front-momentum bar: provinces gained/lost over the last 7 days rendered as a diverging bar (green right = you advancing). Update on your existing hourly tick. Every figure hovers to a breakdown (per-theater, per-army). This is ~1 aggregation query over data you already have, and directly answers 'overall army numbers' + 'estimates of enemy losses' in one strip.

findings.name: Zoom-level LOD: aggregate counters, never shrink them; 4,600 provinces demands it
findings.detail: HoI4 merges division counters into army and theater counters as you zoom out (count rolls up, bars average); DEFCON stays legible at planetary scale by capping glyph count and letting density, not detail, carry information. The failure mode to avoid is Paradox's own early one: counters that scale down with zoom until bars are 1px and unreadable — the mods that fix this ('bigger strength and organisation bars, tidier layout') are among the most subscribed.
findings.recommendation: Fix counter screen-size (28px) at all zooms and change WHAT they represent instead: zoom tier A (province) = one counter per province with pips-chip on hover; tier B (region) = one counter per army/front segment, count = total divisions, bars = weighted averages, worst-supply alert pip wins; tier C (strategic) = one counter per theater + front line only. Front line itself: render the contact line between hostile provinces as a 3px polyline in the two nation colors offset 1.5px each side, and where it moved in the last 48h, draw the old position as a 1px dashed trail — the trail IS the 'who is winning' answer at strategic zoom, no numbers needed.

key_takeaways: Ship four things TODAY, in this order of leverage: (1) strength+cohesion bars on every counter (HoI4 dual-bar — maps 1:1 onto your cohesion-vs-strength model), (2) on-map battle bubbles with a green/red predicted-outcome arc, (3) movement arrows + ghost counters for units in transit (kills 'troops appear by magic'), (4) a combat window whose modifier ledger prints signed green/red percentages with a one-line plain-language verdict ('losing because entrenchment -25% and river -30%').

Counter spec: 28px fixed-screen-size nation-color rounded rect, white NATO glyph (X saltire infantry / oval armor / dot artillery), stack count pill top-right, size designator above frame, bottom horizontal strength bar (3px, green/yellow/red ramp) + left vertical cohesion bar (3px, cyan→orange ramp), max ONE alert pip. Must read in grayscale; color is redundant, never load-bearing.

Three-tier disclosure, strictly: map counter answers 'where is the problem' (bars + alert pip only), hover card (<100ms) answers 'what is here' (per-division rows with bars + incoming reinforcements ETA), click panel answers 'what do I do' (full stats, modifiers, orders). Anything that can't justify its tier gets demoted, per Unity of Command's praised minimalism — its chips work because strength is 5-7 countable pips (subitizable), not a number; use pip-chips as the mid-zoom/hover state.

Fog with visible uncertainty: enemy counts quantized (1-3/4-8/9+), enemy bars in thirds and dimmed, enemy losses shown as intel-scaled ranges ('~8,000–12,000') that sharpen with intel — WitE's '?-?' principle: display precision must encode information quality. You already know the truth; add rounding tiers, don't fabricate a new system.

Who-is-winning at map scale without numbers: battle-bubble arc color per fight, and at strategic zoom a 3px two-tone front line whose 48h-old position renders as a dashed trail — the gap between line and trail IS the momentum display. Plus a persistent war ribbon: troops/divisions both sides, cumulative losses (yours exact, theirs est.), and a 7-day provinces-gained diverging bar, updated on the existing hourly tick.

LOD by aggregation, never by shrinking: province counters → army counters → theater counters as zoom decreases, all at 28px; the #1 community fix to HoI4's counters is 'bigger bars, tidier layout' — do not repeat Paradox's 1px-bar mistake across 4,600 provinces.

Sources: gamedeveloper.com/design/design-case-study-unity-of-command · en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NATO_Joint_Military_Symbology · lparchive.org/War-in-the-East-Don-to-the-Danube/Update 01 (counter tutorial) · dornshuld.chemistry.msstate.edu/rules/wite2/6-0.html (WitE2 UI manual, via search excerpt) · hoi4.paradoxwikis.com/Land_battle · steamcommunity.com MPU Map Counters (1359910088) and DzK Better Counters (699668071) mod pages · explorminate.org/unity-of-command-ii-review

reports.topic: War information design: battle inspection UI, pre-battle forecasting, and "why am I losing" transparency for an hourly-tick Cold War grand strategy game

findings.name: Battle window anatomy: mirrored two-column layout with a central balance-of-power bar (HoI4's best-liked element)
findings.detail: HoI4's land battle window is the genre reference: attacker column left, defender column right, a horizontal balance-of-power bar in the middle with a predicted-winner indicator, division rows beneath each side showing per-division org (green) and strength (yellow) bars, and a modifier icon strip whose tooltips explain terrain/river/encirclement/supply penalties. Players consistently praise the at-a-glance bar and per-division bars; they consistently hate that (a) the modifier explanations are buried in hover-only tooltips with no summed numbers visible, (b) there is no end-of-battle casualty report (HoI3 had one and its removal is a top community complaint — 'no way to know if I took heavy casualties'), and (c) the prediction gives no time estimate. EU4's version is worse and worth NOT copying: it shows raw dice and phase bars but hides the actual damage math, so losing feels arbitrary — the classic 'I had more troops, why did I lose?' thread generator.
findings.recommendation: Build a battle window (opens on clicking a contested province or the combat icon on the front line): ~560px wide floating panel. Top: province name + terrain icon + battle duration ('Fighting for 14h'). Center: full-width balance-of-power bar (attacker color left, defender right) computed from total remaining cohesion ratio, with a marker showing projected resolution: 'Defender breaks in ~9h' derived by extrapolating current cohesion delta per tick — you already tick hourly, so this is a trivial linear projection and is the single highest-value number in the whole window. Below, two mirrored columns: total soldiers, total strength, total cohesion (number + bar), effective attack/defense AFTER modifiers with the pre-modifier base in parentheses, e.g. 'Attack 342 (base 480, −29%)'. Under each column, a row of unit chips, one per division: name, quality pips, cohesion bar (green), strength bar (yellow). Keep it under ~8 visible rows with a scroll. On battle end, emit a battle report toast + log entry with casualties both sides, hours fought, and winner — do not skip this; its absence is HoI4's most-cited regression.

findings.name: Modifier list must be visible, summed, signed, and sorted — not tooltip-only
findings.detail: The universal criticism of HoI4/EU4 combat windows is that the 'why' lives in stacked hover tooltips: players can see THAT they're losing but must hover six icons and do mental arithmetic to learn WHY. AGEOD's engine draws the same complaint ('results of some battles are not understood'). War in the East is the opposite extreme — an exhaustive post-battle text dump that only grognards read. The winning middle ground is a visible, pre-summed modifier ledger.
findings.recommendation: In each column of the battle window, render a plain visible list (no hover required) of every active modifier as a signed percentage, sorted by absolute magnitude, colored red/green: 'Terrain: Mountains −40% · Attacking across river −25% · Home ground +15% · Unit quality +10% · Net −40%'. Cap at 5 rows + 'and 2 more…' expander. Then add the killer feature no Paradox game has: a one-line auto-diagnosis at the bottom of the window that names the top decisive factor by comparing the two nets, e.g. 'You are losing primarily because of the Mountain terrain penalty (−40%). Enemy quality also exceeds yours (+10% vs −5%).' Compute it as: take the largest |modifier| gap between sides plus the raw-strength ratio; template a sentence. This single label answers the director's 'why am I losing' verbatim and costs ~50 lines of code.

findings.name: Yes, show a pre-battle forecast — UoC-style odds are the most praised feature in the genre; ItB proves 'consequences beat probabilities'
findings.detail: Unity of Command's pre-attack combat sheet (predicted kills/suppression shown as pips before you commit) is the most-praised combat UI in wargaming; reviews specifically credit 'odds clearly presented, easy to see if an attack is worth trying.' Notably, UoC2's dev REMOVED the abstract odds number because new players found it 'obscure and confusing', kept the concrete outcome preview, then re-added the number as an opt-in after veteran demand — the lesson is: forecast in concrete units (losses, time), not abstract ratios. UoC also randomizes around the forecast with a narrow distribution, so the preview is honest but not deterministic. Into the Breach's postmortem doubles down: telegraph outcomes so 'every death feels like the player's own fault.' A grand strategy game can't be fully deterministic, but hourly cohesion attrition is smooth and highly predictable — hiding the projection just makes the sim feel like magic.
findings.recommendation: Two forecasts. (1) Pre-battle: when the player hovers/selects an attack order into a province, show a compact forecast card: predicted outcome verb + confidence ('Likely victory', 'Even fight', 'Likely defeat' — 5 buckets), estimated duration ('~2 days'), estimated own losses and enemy losses as ranges ('your losses 800–1,400'), and the top 2 modifiers that drive it ('Mountains −40%'). Compute by running the actual combat formula forward with current values — since combat is deterministic-ish per tick, simulate N ticks headlessly; if there's RNG, run 20 quick rollouts and report the spread. Never show a bare ratio like '3:2'. (2) In-battle: the same projection updates live in the battle window ('Defender breaks in ~9h' / 'You will break first — in ~6h'). Do NOT make the forecast account for enemy reserves the player can't see (fog honesty, see enemy-intel finding); label it 'assuming no reinforcements'.

findings.name: Kill the 'troops appear by magic' problem with provenance arrows and a live reserves/reinforcement ledger
findings.detail: The director's 'where troops come from (seems like magic!)' is exactly the AGEOD community's top battle-report request: 'no information about which stacks started the battle and which are added and withdrawing.' HoI4 partially solves this with battle-plan arrows and a 'reserves' section in the combat window (divisions listed as not-yet-deployed with a join chance), plus small arrows on the map showing which provinces each engaged division fights FROM. Players rely on these heavily.
findings.recommendation: Three mechanisms. (1) In the battle window, split each side's unit list into 'Engaged' and 'Arriving' sections; each Arriving row shows origin province and ETA in hours ('4th Rifle Div — from Brno, arrives 7h'). (2) On the map while a battle is selected, draw thin arrows from each contributing province to the battle province, colored per side — this makes force flow legible at a glance and reuses your existing province adjacency data. (3) Keep a per-battle event log (ring buffer, ~20 entries) rendered as a collapsible strip at the window bottom: '06:00 3rd Tank Div joined from Plzeň · 14:00 2nd Inf Div withdrew (cohesion broken)'. Every unit that enters or leaves a battle appends one line. This is the full answer to 'magic' and also becomes your battle-report data source.

findings.name: Enemy loss estimates: show them as intel-quality ranges, War-in-the-East style, never exact
findings.detail: War in the East displays enemy combat values and casualties through a fog-of-war filter — you see detection-level-degraded numbers (often bracketed/rounded), and its combat report shows both sides' losses after every battle; grognards praise that losses are always reported even if fuzzed. HoI4 shows exact enemy losses in the battle window, which players like but which removes any intelligence gameplay. For a Cold War game, fuzzy-but-visible enemy losses are thematically perfect (Order of Battle intelligence was THE Cold War obsession).
findings.recommendation: Always show an enemy-losses figure in the battle window and in war-level aggregates, but as a range whose width scales with an intel quality score (even a constant 'recon' stat per side works for v1): high intel → '~2,300 (±10%)', low intel → '1,500–4,000'. Implementation: track true enemy losses, display value = true ± noise sampled once per battle (not per frame, or the number jitters), range width from intel. In the war-room panel add a cumulative scoreboard: 'Your losses 48,200 (exact) · Enemy losses est. 61,000–75,000'. Rounding rule: never render fuzzed numbers with more than 2 significant figures — '61,000', not '61,342' — false precision destroys the fiction.

findings.name: Map layer: per-province troop counts and a front-line strength strip (the 'watching a war' view)
findings.detail: The director wants to WATCH wars: troops per province and overall army numbers. HoI4's solution is counters/NATO sprites per province plus a front-line ribbon with per-front division counts and army HUD at screen bottom; its army-view map mode dims everything but military info. The current 'small colored boxes with a count' is the right primitive but carries no strength/cohesion information, so a province with 3 elite full-strength divisions looks identical to 3 broken ones.
findings.recommendation: (1) Upgrade the province counter: a small stack chip showing division count + total manpower (rounded: '12k'), with a 2px cohesion bar underneath colored green→yellow→red — now the map itself shows where the line is about to break. Aggregate chips when zoomed out (sum per front segment). (2) Battles get a distinct pulsing crossed-swords marker on the contested province edge; clicking opens the battle window. (3) Add an 'army numbers' header strip to the existing war-room panel: for each side, total soldiers, total divisions, front-line average cohesion, and losses to date — four numbers per side, updated per tick, no scrolling. (4) Optional but cheap and very Cold-War: a war-room 'front graph' — a sparkline of total front-line strength ratio over the last 30 days, so the player sees the tide turning before provinces flip.

findings.name: Hourly ticks: render the tick stream as deltas and sparklines, not dice
findings.detail: EU4 shows literal dice each phase and players find it flavorful but uninformative — the die tells you nothing actionable and obscures the modifier math. HoI4 hides its hourly rolls entirely and shows only bar movement, which reads as smooth but opaque. Since this game's combat is cohesion-vs-strength attrition per hour, the per-tick delta IS the legible unit of information.
findings.recommendation: In the battle window, next to each side's cohesion total, show the current per-hour delta ('−1.8/h') and a 24-tick sparkline of cohesion history. When a delta's sign or magnitude changes materially (reinforcement arrived, posture changed, terrain modifier changed), the event log entry explains it. This gives the player the HoI4 'watch the bars fight' pleasure plus the causality HoI4 hides. Skip any dice imagery entirely — with hourly ticks and modifiers, randomness (if any) should be presented as the forecast range, not as per-tick theater.

findings.name: Implementation priority order for a same-day build
findings.detail: Everything above ranks by (player value ÷ implementation cost) given the described codebase: combat values already exist per tick, so most of this is presentation. The forecast simulation reuses the combat step function; the diagnosis line reuses the modifier list; arrows reuse adjacency; the report reuses the event log.
findings.recommendation: Ship in this order: 1) Battle window with mirrored columns, visible signed modifier ledger, balance bar, and 'breaks in ~Nh' projection (core, ~a day). 2) 'Why you are losing' auto-diagnosis line (trivial once ledger exists). 3) Engaged/Arriving split + battle event log (kills the 'magic'). 4) War-room aggregate numbers + fuzzed enemy loss ranges. 5) Map counter upgrade with cohesion bar + battle markers + provenance arrows. 6) Pre-battle forecast card on attack-order hover (needs headless rollout plumbing — do last). Defer: front strength sparkline, end-of-battle report polish.

key_takeaways: Copy HoI4's battle-window skeleton (mirrored columns + central balance bar + per-division cohesion/strength bars) but fix its two famous sins: surface modifiers as a visible signed, sorted ledger instead of hover tooltips, and always produce an end-of-battle casualty report.
The single highest-value number is a live time-to-resolution projection ('Defender breaks in ~9h') — trivially computable from the hourly cohesion delta the sim already produces.
Answer 'why am I losing' literally: an auto-generated one-line diagnosis naming the biggest modifier gap between the two sides ('losing primarily due to Mountains −40%').

Yes to pre-battle forecasts — Unity of Command proves they're beloved — but forecast in concrete units (predicted losses range, duration, outcome bucket like 'Likely defeat'), never abstract odds ratios, and label them 'assuming no reinforcements'.

Kill 'troops from magic' with three things: Engaged vs Arriving (origin + ETA) sections in the battle window, thin origin-arrows on the map while a battle is selected, and a per-battle join/withdraw event log.
Show enemy losses always, but as intel-quality-scaled ranges rounded to 2 significant figures (War in the East fog model) — thematically perfect for Cold War OOB-intelligence fantasy.

Upgrade map province counters from 'colored box + count' to count + manpower + a 2px cohesion bar, and add a 4-number-per-side aggregate strip (soldiers, divisions, avg cohesion, losses) to the existing war-room panel.
No dice theater: with hourly ticks, express randomness as forecast ranges and per-hour delta sparklines; per-tick RNG display (EU4 dice) is flavor without information.

reports.topic: War information design for a Cold War grand strategy game: war-level dashboards, fog-of-war intelligence estimates, loss reporting, and troop-provenance UI (research from HoI4, Vic3, EU4, Twilight Struggle, WitP, Flashpoint Campaigns)

findings.name: HoI4 war overview: the baseline dashboard shape that works
findings.detail: HoI4's war overview lists each war with both sides' participants sorted by war-participation %, a per-nation surrender-limit progress bar, and aggregate casualties per side. Participation is a hoverable number decomposed into occupation points, land-combat damage dealt, and casualties suffered (every 1000 own casualties = 0.5 warscore; occupation of provinces weighted by state value/victory points). The key lesson: every headline number is a hover-decomposable sum, and per-NATION bars (not just per-side) let you see WHICH ally is collapsing. Sources: https://hoi4.paradoxwikis.com/War_participation , https://hoi4.paradoxwikis.com/War , https://steamcommunity.com/app/394360/discussions/0/1734333281937481252/
findings.recommendation: Restructure the war-room panel into three stacked zones. Zone 1 (header, ~64px): war name, start date, elapsed days, and one big momentum number (see warscore finding). Zone 2 (participants table): one row per belligerent, columns = flag/name | divisions committed | manpower committed | casualties | contribution %; sort by contribution descending; give each nation a thin (4px) 'war exhaustion / surrender progress' bar under its row. Zone 3 (theater summary): per-front stats. Every aggregate number gets a tooltip that lists its top 5 contributing terms with values — build the tooltip from the same accumulator structs used in the sim, never a second codepath.

findings.name: EU4 warscore breakdown: momentum must be an explained, decomposed score
findings.detail: EU4's war screen sums warscore from discrete sources — battles won (scaled by battle size vs total forces), provinces occupied (scaled by development, forts and capitals weighted), blockades, plus a ticking component from holding the war goal (max 25%), shown as a green/red arrow you hover for the monthly tick. Players consistently report that the breakdown-on-hover is what makes the number trustworthy; confusion arises exactly where components are hidden. Sources: https://forum.paradoxplaza.com/forum/threads/need-help-understanding-war-score.1548992/ , https://steamcommunity.com/app/236850/discussions/0/135514766277682419/
findings.recommendation: Add a single -100..+100 'War Momentum' score at the top of the panel, computed from explicit weighted terms: net provinces (occupation value), net casualties inflicted (exchange ratio vs manpower pools), front movement over last 30 days, and strategic objectives held. Render as a horizontal tug-of-war bar (own color left, enemy right) with a small arrow glyph showing 7-day trend direction; tooltip lists each term with its signed value ('Occupation +18, Casualty exchange -6, Front movement +3'). This is the single number that answers 'am I winning?', and the tooltip answers 'why?'.

findings.name: Vic3 war panel: the anti-pattern list (what the director's complaint sounds like)
findings.detail: Vic3's warfare UI is the canonical failure case and matches the director's complaint almost verbatim: critical info buried in nested panels, battles spawn with seemingly random troop counts drawn from a front pool (player outnumbers 3:1 but battles land at parity with no explanation), and no feedback loop showing whether an order helped ('not seeing anything to indicate whether that was a good or bad choice'). Paradox's own fix direction was consolidating scattered info into fewer, more obvious locations and single rich tooltips. 'Where troops come from (seems like magic)' is exactly the Vic3 front-pool opacity problem. Sources: https://forum.paradoxplaza.com/forum/threads/should-the-victoria-3-warfare-system-be-state-based-instead-of-front-based.1556253/page-3 , https://steamcommunity.com/app/529340/discussions/0/3470612993471891285/
findings.recommendation: Three hard rules: (1) any number the sim uses in the hourly combat tick must be inspectable in exactly one click or hover from the map or war panel; (2) never teleport or silently pool units — every division that arrives in a battle/province must have a visible origin and travel path; (3) after any player order (posture change, reinforcement), the UI must show a delta within a few ticks (e.g. posture change → projected front-strength change shown immediately). Implement (2) as movement arrows on the map: when a division is in transit, draw a tapered arrow from origin province to destination, colored by owner, with an ETA-in-hours label; hovering a province's unit stack lists each division with 'arrived from Kraków, Aug 12' provenance.

findings.name: HoI4 intel tiers: the concrete model for enemy numbers under fog
findings.detail: HoI4 displays enemy army data as tiered, progressively-narrowing estimates driven by an Army Intel 0-100% stat: at 0-10% intel, total fielded division count is shown with ±80% uncertainty; ~20-30% reveals which templates exist but counts stay ±100%; 50%+ gives division-count-by-template and equipment ratios; 70%+ exact fielded counts; 80%+ exact template internals. Intel accrues from spy networks, radar coverage, broken ciphers, recon aircraft, and — importantly — from combat itself (fighting the enemy reveals them). The side with more intel also gets a flat combat-stat bonus. Sources: https://hoi4.paradoxwikis.com/Intel , https://forum.paradoxplaza.com/forum/threads/hoi4-dev-diary-intel.1295585/
findings.recommendation: Implement a per-enemy-country IntelLevel (0-100) driven by: adjacency/contact on a front (+), active combat (+, fastest), recon flights over territory (+ for that region), elapsed time without contact (decay). Display enemy strength as a range whose width is a function of intel: width_pct = max(5, 100 - intel). Format as rounded brackets, never fake precision: '~40-60 divisions' at low intel, '~48-52' at high, exact '50' only above ~90. Round range endpoints to sensible steps (5s or 10s). Per-province enemy counters show a band ('2-4 div') below high intel, exact count above. Store true value and estimate separately — the estimate is a sampled belief (true ± noise scaled by uncertainty) that only re-samples on new sightings, so the number doesn't jitter every tick.

findings.name: WitP claimed-vs-confirmed losses: how to display estimated enemy casualties
findings.detail: War in the Pacific is the reference for loss estimation under fog: combat reports show CLAIMED enemy losses that are systematically inflated (pilots overclaim, jittery spotters turn cruisers into carriers), and sighting reports carry explicit inaccuracy — an observed task force yields a report that is truthful, exaggerated, underestimated, or outright false depending on observer quality (land observers/subs accurate, aircraft unreliable). Its intel screen tracks enemy losses as running estimates distinct from ground truth, and veteran players learn to mentally discount claims — the game makes overclaiming itself a knowable, learnable bias. Sources: https://forums.matrixgames.com/viewtopic.php?t=371632 , https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/War_in_the_Pacific_(board_game)
findings.recommendation: Track three loss numbers per enemy: true losses (sim-internal, never shown), claimed losses (sum of per-battle claims, generated by inflating true battle losses by a factor drawn from ~1.2-2.0x, lower for battles you won and held the ground — you can count wrecks — higher for battles you lost or long-range attrition), and confirmed losses (true losses in battles where you held the field afterward, plus captured-province garrisons). Display in the war panel as 'Enemy losses: 12,400 confirmed / est. 18,000-31,000 total' with the estimate range derived from claims discounted by current intel level. Own losses are always exact. This one line — confirmed vs estimated with a range — directly answers 'estimates of enemy losses' and creates the classic Cold War texture of contested body counts.

findings.name: Sighting staleness: last-seen timestamps and ghost markers (Flashpoint Campaigns / WitP pattern)
findings.detail: Tactical wargames with serious FOW (Flashpoint Campaigns, WitP) treat every enemy marker as a report with an age: contacts are per-sensor sightings that decay, and a marker where the enemy WAS is visually distinct from a live contact. Flashpoint's spotting is per-sensor (radar/thermal/optical) and contact info degrades to stale markers; WitP task-force sightings carry a report time and become progressively less trustworthy. The generalizable principle: never show enemy positions as timeless facts — show them as dated reports. Sources: https://forums.matrixgames.com/viewtopic.php?t=389950 , https://steamcommunity.com/app/330720/discussions/0/1651045226236834398/
findings.recommendation: Every enemy unit marker off the active front carries a last-seen age. Rendering: fresh (<24h) markers at full opacity with solid border; 1-7 days at ~60% opacity with dashed border and a small '3d' age label; >7 days become a hollow 'ghost' outline at the last-known province (question-mark glyph), and disappear entirely after ~30 days. Enemy units in direct front contact are always fresh. Hover text: 'Est. 2-4 divisions, last confirmed 3 days ago (air recon)'. This is cheap to implement (one timestamp + one enum per known-enemy-unit record) and single-handedly makes fog feel designed rather than broken.

findings.name: Twilight Struggle: strategic-layer openness is period-authentic for the Cold War
findings.detail: Twilight Struggle — the definitive Cold War game — uses almost fully open information: board state, influence, scoring conditions and ops values are all public; the only hidden info is the opponent's hand (intentions, not capabilities). Its tension comes from uncertainty about what the opponent will DO, not what they HAVE. This mirrors reality: by the 1950s-60s, order-of-battle intelligence at the strategic level (how many divisions the USSR fields overall) was roughly known to both sides via national technical means, while tactical dispositions and readiness were murky. Design implication: hiding strategic aggregates frustrates without adding period flavor; the interesting fog is at the operational level.
findings.recommendation: Adopt a two-tier fog policy. STRATEGIC aggregates are near-open: total enemy army size, total manpower pool, and cumulative war losses always visible as ranges (tight ones — ±10-20% even at zero effort, representing signals intelligence and attaché reporting). OPERATIONAL detail is fogged hard: which provinces enemy divisions sit in, their cohesion/quality, and reserves behind the front use the full intel-tier + staleness treatment. This gives the director his 'overall army numbers' immediately for both sides without any intel grind, while keeping map-level surprise. It also means the war panel's participants table can always be fully populated (enemy rows just show ranges and a small 'est.' tag in the corner of each cell).

findings.name: 'Why am I losing': per-battle modifier ledger and aggregated attribution
findings.detail: The director's 'why am I losing' maps to two granularities the sim already computes: per-battle (cohesion-vs-strength with terrain/home/quality modifiers) and war-level (aggregate patterns). HoI4's combat interface shows both sides' widths, org/strength bars, and a full list of signed percentage modifiers per side; its weakness is that nothing aggregates across battles, so players still can't see systemic causes. Vic3's failure was the opposite — outcomes with no visible inputs at all.
findings.recommendation: Two features. (a) Battle inspector: clicking a contested province shows both sides' committed divisions (yours exact, enemy as estimate), each side's total effective strength as base x listed modifiers ('Base 12,000 x 0.8 terrain (mountains) x 1.1 home x 0.95 low cohesion = 10,032 eff.'), with the deciding disadvantage highlighted in red. Since combat ticks hourly, also show a mini sparkline of relative strength over the battle's life. (b) War-level 'Assessment' box in the war panel: aggregate the modifier ledger across all battles of the last 30 days and emit the top 2-3 systemic causes as plain sentences chosen by largest summed negative contribution: 'You are losing battles primarily due to terrain (attacking into mountains, -22% avg) and troop quality (-15% avg). Numbers are roughly even.' This turns the existing sim math into an answer instead of asking the player to reverse-engineer it.

findings.name: Map-level troop counts per province: numbers on counters, aggregated by zoom
findings.detail: Small colored boxes with a count (current state) hide the two things players scan for: relative mass along a front and quality/state. Established solutions: HoI4 shows per-province army counters with division counts and aggregates them into army groups at low zoom; classic hex wargames print strength-cohesion factors directly on counters; Flashpoint renders unit state (moving/dug-in/broken) as small pips on the marker.
findings.recommendation: Upgrade the province counter to a 3-element chip (~44x28px at standard zoom): division count in large text, a 3px strength bar underneath (fill = avg strength %, color shifts green->amber->red), and a 3px cohesion bar below that in a second hue. Enemy chips show the ranged count ('2-4') and drop the bars below ~50 intel, showing a '?' pip instead. At far zoom, merge chips along a front into per-front totals ('NATO 38 | 41-55 PACT' floating on the front line). Add a 'front strength ribbon': a thin colored band drawn along the front line itself, width or color-intensity proportional to local force ratio, so a glance shows where you're thin — this is the fastest possible answer to 'why am I losing HERE'.

findings.name: Troop provenance: reinforcement ticker and origin tracking (killing the 'magic')
findings.detail: 'Where troops come from (seems like magic)' has two failure sources: units moving without visible transit (teleport perception) and no event trail for arrivals. Grand-strategy games that avoid this (HoI4) draw movement arrows with progress for every moving division and keep an accessible unit history; games that fail (Vic3 fronts) pool units invisibly. Real-time-with-pause plus hourly ticks means arrivals happen while the player watches elsewhere, so a passive log is required, not just live arrows.
findings.recommendation: Three pieces, all cheap given per-division entities: (1) transit arrows as specified above (origin->destination, ETA label); (2) a per-division provenance field (last 3 waypoints + timestamps) surfaced in unit tooltips; (3) a war-event ticker in the war panel — a scrolling list (newest on top, ~6 visible rows, 22px each) of timestamped events: 'Aug 12 06:00 — 2nd Guards Div arrived at Brno from Bratislava', 'Aug 12 09:00 — Battle of Brno begun (est. 3-5 enemy div)', 'Aug 13 — Pilsen captured'. Enemy arrival events only fire when intel/staleness rules would reveal them ('New enemy formation detected near Dresden — est. 2-3 divisions'). The ticker doubles as the war's narrative memory and is where 'losing' becomes a story the player can read backwards.

findings.name: The summary stat row: numbers that make a war feel trackable
findings.detail: Across the surveyed games, wars feel legible when a small fixed set of aggregates is always visible and each moves on a human-perceivable timescale: HoI4's surrender-limit bars and casualty totals, EU4's warscore + ticking arrow, wargame AAR culture's exchange ratios and front-movement talk ('the front hasn't moved in a month' is how real players narrate wars). Derived/tempo stats (days since front moved, 7-day exchange ratio) are absent from all Paradox titles and are the most-requested texture in AAR/forum discussions — they convert an hourly-tick sim's noise into perceived momentum.
findings.recommendation: Pin a stat strip across the top of the war panel — six tiles, ~110x64px each, big number + tiny label + 7-day trend arrow: (1) Momentum score (the tug-of-war bar); (2) Provinces taken/lost, shown net with total ('+12 net, 31 taken / 19 lost'); (3) Your casualties (exact) vs (4) Enemy casualties ('9,100 confirmed / est. 14-22k'); (5) Manpower committed vs available ('310k of 840k') for each side (enemy as range); (6) Front tempo: 'Front moved 40km west / 7d' or the stagnation counter 'Front static 23 days'. All six are computable from state the sim already has plus one ring buffer of daily snapshots (province ownership set, casualty totals, front centroid) — keep 90 daily snapshots per war and every trend/tempo stat falls out of diffs.

key_takeaways: Build the war panel as: header with a decomposable -100..+100 momentum tug-of-war bar, a six-tile stat strip (momentum, net provinces, own casualties, est. enemy casualties, manpower committed, days-since-front-moved), a per-nation participants table with contribution % and exhaustion bars, and a timestamped war-event ticker. A 90-day ring buffer of daily war snapshots powers every trend stat.

Two-tier fog, Cold War authentic (Twilight Struggle logic): strategic aggregates (enemy total army size, manpower, cumulative losses) always visible as tight ranges with an 'est.' tag; operational detail (which provinces, cohesion, reserves) gated by a 0-100 per-country intel level that grows from front contact/combat/recon and decays with time.

Enemy numbers are always ranges whose width shrinks with intel (HoI4 model: ±80% at low intel down to exact above ~90), rounded to clean steps, backed by a sampled-belief value that only re-samples on new sightings so displayed estimates don't jitter each tick.

Enemy losses display as 'X confirmed / est. Y-Z total' (WitP model): confirmed = true losses where you held the battlefield or captured the province; estimated = inflated per-battle claims (1.2-2.0x) discounted by intel. Own losses always exact. Never show the true number.

Every enemy marker is a dated report, not a fact: last-seen age drives opacity/dashed-border/ghost-outline rendering and appears in the tooltip ('last confirmed 3 days ago, air recon'); markers expire after ~30 days. Front-contact units are always fresh.

Kill the 'magic troops' complaint with provenance: transit arrows with ETA for every moving division, a last-3-waypoints history in unit tooltips, and arrival events in the war ticker — enemy arrivals fire detection events only when intel rules reveal them.

Answer 'why am I losing' at two levels: a battle inspector showing each side's effective strength as base x listed modifiers with the worst one highlighted, and a war-level Assessment box that aggregates modifier contributions across 30 days of battles into 2-3 plain-language causes ('losing primarily due to terrain, -22% avg').

Avoid the Vic3 anti-patterns explicitly: no sim-relevant number more than one hover away, no invisible pooling/teleporting of units, and every player order must produce a visible delta within a few ticks.

reports.topic: War information design: making troops legible — manpower pipeline (population → pool → field strength → casualties), reinforcement mechanics, and combat/war-room UI specs from HoI4, Victoria 2, and War in the East

findings.name: Minimum viable reinforcement mechanic: national pool + 10%-increment strength regen (HoI4 model)
findings.detail: HoI4's pipeline: sum of controlled-state populations × conscription-law percentage (Volunteer 1.5% → Extended 5% → Scraping the Barrel 25%) = recruitable manpower; it enters the 'free' pool over time via mobilization speed (a ramp, not instant); divisions below full strength automatically request reinforcements from the free pool 'as long as they have a supply line back to the capital', and 'reinforcements arrive in increments of 10% of the division's full manpower'. Casualties instantly deduct from the division and are gone. Free manpower sits in the top-left bar; hover gives a per-branch free/used breakdown. When the pool hits zero, divisions silently stop refilling — a notorious legibility failure players complain about ('why won't my divisions reinforce?'). Sources: https://hoi4.paradoxwikis.com/Manpower , https://gamerempire.net/hearts-of-iron-4-how-to-increase-manpower/
findings.recommendation: Implement today, ~1 system + 1 resource: `ManpowerPool { available: f64, mobilizing: f64, fielded: f64, dead: f64 }` per nation. Daily tick: move `mobilizing * 0.04` into `available` (≈25-day ramp — same constant WitE2 uses for its transit pool). Hourly combat tick already exists — add a daily reinforcement pass: every division with strength < 100% and a supply path draws `min(0.1 × full_strength, pool.available, deficit)`; sort draw order by a per-division priority flag (default: front-line first). Conscription is one enum on the nation (1%/2.5%/5%/10% of population) changed from the war room. Critically: when a draw fails because the pool is empty, set a `starved: bool` on the division and surface it (see UI findings) — never fail silently like HoI4.

findings.name: Victoria 2's soldier POPs: provenance is what kills the 'magic' — tag every division with a home province
findings.detail: Vic2 is the genre's gold standard for 'where do troops come from': each regiment is raised from a specific soldier POP in a specific province (3,000 men per regiment from core states), is named after it, and reinforces ONLY from that POP — when the home population is bled dry, that regiment visibly cannot refill, and dead soldiers actually reduce the home province's population. Players praise exactly this: the army is a projection of real, located people, and attrition has a visible demographic address. Max 5% of a region's population can be soldiers, with diminishing growth near the cap. Sources: https://forum.paradoxplaza.com/forum/threads/how-do-units-soldiers-and-pops-work.962622/ , https://vic2.paradoxwikis.com/National_focus_and_population_guide , https://steamcommunity.com/app/42960/discussions/0/540738051429028690/
findings.recommendation: Cheapest high-impact change in this whole list: add `home_province: ProvinceId` to every division and auto-name divisions from it ('3rd Kharkov Rifles'). With 4,600 provinces you already have the population substrate. You do NOT need full per-POP accounting on day one — keep the single national pool for the mechanic, but debit casualties against `province.population` of the home province and show provenance in the division tooltip: 'Raised: Kharkov (pop 1.34M, −22,400 war dead)'. Later upgrade: reinforcements preferentially drawn from the home region, with a 'depleted region' warning. Also add a map-mode tinting provinces by war dead per capita — this single view answers 'what has this war cost me' better than any table.

findings.name: War in the East's replacement flow: the delay pool and per-unit TOE% readout
findings.detail: WitE2 models men flowing 'from the home front... through intermediate locations such as repair depots and hospitals, to the combat zone': casualties/returning wounded enter a TRANSIT pool, and only 25% of the transit pool moves to the AVAILABLE pool per turn — so losses are not instantly reusable and the player watches the pipeline refill. Units only receive replacements if they can trace supply to a depot with freight and are not isolated; delivery scales with distance and whether the unit moved. Each unit displays a TOE% (current strength vs table-of-organization), the number every WitE player scans to judge readiness. Sources: https://www.dornshuld.chemistry.msstate.edu/rules/wite2/26-0.html , https://dornshuld.com/rules/wite2/25-0.html
findings.recommendation: Adopt two things: (1) the delay pool — your `mobilizing → available` ramp above already gives you this; additionally route a fraction of combat losses (say 20%, 'lightly wounded') back into `mobilizing` rather than `dead`, so the pool visibly partially recovers and the numbers reconcile; (2) the TOE%-style single readiness number: render '82%' next to every division counter's strength bar. Distance/depot logistics is NOT minimum-viable — approximate it with your existing supply-path check plus a flat 'reinforcement rate ×0.5 if >N provinces from a friendly city'.

findings.name: The pipeline display: a four-stage manpower strip in the war room, with reconciling numbers
findings.detail: HoI4 shows only one number (free manpower) in the top bar and hides the pipeline in tooltips — and its players constantly ask why divisions aren't reinforcing. WitE2 shows the pools on a production screen but disconnected from the front. Nobody renders the full flow population → recruitable → mobilizing → fielded → casualties in one glance, which is exactly the director's 'seems like magic' complaint. The fix is a conservation-of-mass display: every man is in exactly one bucket and the buckets visibly sum.
findings.recommendation: Add a horizontal 'Manpower Pipeline' strip at the top of the war-room panel, ~640×64px: five chips connected by arrows — [Population 182M] → [Recruitable 9.1M (5% Conscription ▾)] → [Reserve 1.2M (+38k/day)] → [Fielded 2.6M in 214 divisions] → [Casualties 412k ☠]. Each chip: 11px label above, 20px bold figure, delta-per-day in 10px underneath colored green/red. The Recruitable chip embeds the conscription dropdown so cause and lever live together. Hover any chip → tooltip listing top-5 contributing provinces. When Reserve < 7 days of current burn rate, flash the chip amber and emit a war-room alert 'Reinforcements exhausted in ~5 days' — this is the direct answer to 'why am I losing' when the answer is attrition.

findings.name: Combat legibility ('why am I losing'): HoI4 combat window pattern — dual bars per division + signed modifier list + prediction bar
findings.detail: HoI4's battle window is the reference pattern: two columns (attacker left, defender right), each division as a row with TWO thin stacked bars (green = strength/manpower, orange = organization — your cohesion), a top progress bar predicting the outcome, and hoverable breakdowns where every modifier appears as a signed percentage (terrain −40%, entrenchment +2%/level, etc.). Its weakness: the modifier math lives only in dense tooltips, so mid-tier players still can't answer 'why am I losing'. Community guides all teach the same reading: org bar hits zero → division retreats; strength bar low → division hits weakly. Source: https://hoi4.paradoxwikis.com/Land_battle
findings.recommendation: Build a battle inspector (opens on clicking a contested province), ~360px wide side panel, three sections: (1) header: province name, terrain icon, and a full-width 8px 'balance' bar (your-color vs enemy-color) driven by current cohesion-damage ratio, with projected result text ('Defender holds ~3 days at current rate'); (2) two columns of division rows, each 24px: name, strength bar (green) over cohesion bar (orange), both 4px tall, numeric '8.2k / 74%'; (3) 'Why' box — do better than HoI4: render the top 3 modifiers PER SIDE inline, not in a tooltip, as signed chips sorted by |magnitude|: 'Mountains −35% · Home ground +15% · Veteran +10%', enemy side likewise, and one auto-generated sentence: 'You are losing because enemy quality (+25%) outweighs your terrain bonus (+15%) and your cohesion is falling 2.1×.' You already compute these modifiers; this is pure presentation.

findings.name: Enemy loss estimates: show fogged ranges, not exact numbers, scaled by an intel level
findings.detail: HoI4's war-overview casualties tab shows exact enemy losses side-by-side per belligerent — legible but widely criticized as omniscient. Wargames like WitE2 fog enemy detail by recon level (unit counters show estimated strength that firms up with recon). The satisfying middle: estimates with visible uncertainty that narrows as the war grinds on, which also makes intel a mechanic for free.
findings.recommendation: Track true enemy losses exactly (you already resolve combat), display them rounded: with intel level 0–3 per enemy nation (derive from: at war + battles fought this month), show `round_to_sig_figs(true ± (40%/25%/10%/5%))` as 'est. 120–180k'. Per-battle, the inspector shows today's exchange: 'Your losses 1,240 · Enemy est. ~900–1,400'. In the war room add a 'Losses' tab: side-by-side belligerent table (flag, men lost, divisions destroyed) plus a cumulative dual-line chart of casualties over war duration, 280×120px, your side solid, enemy dashed-with-band. The chart is what communicates 'this war is bleeding me faster than them' — the single most direct answer to the director's 'why am I losing'.

findings.name: Map layer: troops-per-province counters with strength bars, aggregated by zoom
findings.detail: The current 'small colored boxes with a count' is the right skeleton — HoI4/WitE counters succeed by adding one strength indicator to the box and aggregating at distance. With 4,600 provinces the failure mode is counter clutter; HoI4 solves it by collapsing stacks into army-group counters when zoomed out, and offers a dedicated map mode for raw numbers.
findings.recommendation: Upgrade each province counter to: nation-colored 20×14px box, white troop count in thousands ('12' = 12,000), and a 20×3px bar under the box = average strength% of divisions there (green >75, amber 40–75, red <40); add a 2px red left-edge tick when any division is reinforcement-starved (`starved` flag from the mechanic finding). Zoomed out past ~1:8, merge counters per front segment into one badge showing summed thousands. Add a 'Military' map mode: provinces tinted by garrison size (sequential ramp), contested provinces pulsing. Hovering a counter lists divisions with name + home province + strength% — provenance again, three clicks from anywhere.

key_takeaways: Ship the HoI4-minimum mechanic today: one national ManpowerPool (available/mobilizing/fielded/dead), conscription % × population feeds it on a ~25-day ramp, and under-strength divisions with a supply path draw 10% of full strength per day from it. Never fail silently — set and display a 'starved' flag when the pool can't pay.

The 'magic' is fixed by provenance, not simulation depth: Victoria 2's lesson is that tagging each division with a home province, naming it after that province, and debiting casualties against that province's population makes armies feel real for almost zero engineering cost.

Answer 'where do troops come from' with a conservation-of-mass UI: a five-chip pipeline strip in the war room (Population → Recruitable → Reserve → Fielded → Casualties) with per-day deltas, the conscription lever embedded in the Recruitable chip, and an amber alert when Reserve < 7 days of burn rate.

Answer 'why am I losing' with a battle inspector that renders dual strength/cohesion bars per division AND puts the top-3 signed modifiers per side inline (not in tooltips), plus one generated sentence naming the dominant factor — HoI4 computes this but hides it; hiding it is its biggest UI failure.

Answer 'enemy losses' with fogged ranges (±40% → ±5% by intel level, rounded to significant figures) and a cumulative dual-line casualty chart in the war room — the trend line, not the number, tells the player who is winning the attrition war.
Map fix is incremental: add a 3px strength bar and a red 'starved' tick to the existing province counter boxes, aggregate counters when zoomed out, and add a garrison-size map mode.

Skip for now: per-province soldier POPs, depot/freight logistics, equipment pools, training XP — all are post-MVP; the pipeline strip + provenance tags + battle inspector cover every clause of the director's complaint.
